1. **Seam holes ("rods") along a diagonal two part triangles share.** `core/src/voxel/voxelize.cpp:338-351`: the column's
   point-in-triangle test is "boundary-inclusive" on each triangle's own edge functions, with no tie rule. A column centre that
   lies exactly on the diagonal shared by two triangles of one face can come out a hair outside BOTH (most likely: the shared edge
   is computed from each triangle's own vertex order, so the rounding differs; not yet traced in core), so that face adds no crossing; the winding fill
   (`:361-389`, `above != 0`) then reads the whole column as Empty. Your pad at **Balanced**: 6 empty columns on x = y,
   **(3,3) (12,12) (20,20) (23,23) (26,26) (29,29)**, all 20 layers, owner -1 (114 voxels). **Fast and Fine are clean.** The app
   puts those voxels back for the preview only (`FlexibleLatticeBuilder.inputs(seamFill:)`, U1, `testNoRodsInTheLattice`;
   RED `seamFill: false` = the 6 columns); core's own output keeps the holes. The same bug is behind the E1 review's "Balanced
   diagonal holes" (one-voxel holes along your Top's triangle diagonal) and the lattice stop's two tolerances (two voxels at the
   entry, one voxel's diagonal inside: re-measure both once this is fixed). Fix needed: a watertight tie rule (e.g. top-left)
   in the edge test.

The thread count is also process-wide (`:219`). The app keeps its own solves apart, but can't see the octet's or Organic's.

A Topology run left GenEO on, and the squish sim's fallback then took 73-75 s instead of about 4 s. The stall flag is per thread (`multigrid.cpp:149-150`).

**Mechanism.**
- **`FlexibleEditedFaces`** is pure and memoised on B5's table version, the mesh signature and the paint. It exposes `leaves`, `id(face:point:)`, `leaves(ofFace:)`, `leaves(ofRegion:)`, `successors(of:)`, `wire` and the effective mesh.
- **`FlexibleRegions`** is its only adapter.
- **Ids** (unedited bytes are kept):
  - An unedited, identity, STL or painted face keeps its run id.
  - A cut piece is 1M+rid, and a combined face is 1M+union rid.
  - A Flexible sector is 2M+n.
- **No schema change.** Stale ids are carried at open.

Your words of ~03:05: "temperature also needs a grade... also, what's the difference between "temperature" and "nozzle"
shouldn't they be the same???" then "Temperature needs a grade **option**". They were the same thing: the nozzle temperature
(varioShore foams more when hotter, so it prints softer). Showing two rows was a bug.

What you get, in plain words:
- **One row, "Nozzle °C", under More, in Auto and in Manual.** It is the same place and look in both modes. Auto keeps its Auto
  chip; Manual shows only the tested temperatures (NG_01, NG_02). The Model card's "Temperature" row is gone, and so is the second
  stored value: a pick in Manual is the same setting Auto shows.
- **Grade [Off | On] under it.** When on, it adds three rows:
  - From °C · bottom (the first layer);
  - To °C · top (the last layer);
  - Style: Default (changes a little every layer) or Stepped (bands).
  It runs up the BUILD HEIGHT, because a nozzle only changes temperature between layers. Switched on, From starts at the row's
  temperature and To at the next tested temperature above it.
- **The squish estimate and the views use each layer's temperature.** Your pad in Manual, 190 → 220 °C: the deepest estimate goes
  from 1.69 mm (190 °C everywhere) to 3.37 mm. Per layer, the lattice's stiffness against the 190 °C solve is 0.94 at 2 mm,
  0.72 at 9 mm and 0.42 at 19 mm (hotter layers squish more). Between 190, 220 and 240 °C it is interpolated; past them it is
  extrapolated and the card says "Estimate past tested data (190–240 °C)".
- **A line with the heights for your slicer** (44 characters a line, two lines at most):
  - Stepped: "190 °C to 10 mm · 220 °C";
  - Default: "190 °C at the bed → 240 °C at 20 mm" / "+5 °C every 2 mm up the part".
- **Auto:** the grade drives Auto's display sim the same way (no rebuild: the sims re-solve). Core's job still carries one
  temperature, so the card adds "Shown in the sim only · core's job: one °C". Auto's job bytes are unchanged. CORE LIST item 14.

Decisions made here (yours to overturn):
- Stepped makes one band per ~25 °C, 2 to 4 bands of equal height: 190 → 220 gives 2, 190 → 240 gives 3 (190 / 215 / 240).
- Heights are measured from the part's lowest point along the build direction (its mesh).
- From / To can be set from 180 to 260 °C.
- varioShore is not in order with temperature: 240 °C is a little FIRMER than 220 °C. A 220 → 240 grade barely changes anything.
- Core never interpolates between temperatures (R10). This interpolation is the display sim's own, said here and in the (i).
- The grade row is titled "Grade", the same word as the lattice's Grade above it on the Model card in Manual (NG_01). It sits
  right under "Nozzle °C".
- Found while testing: quick re-solves (Stepped on/off) could leave the sims "working…" for ever. An older hand-over could
  schedule last, and every answer it got was discarded. Fixed: a hand-over checks its own epoch (`startSquishSims`).

Tests (`FlexibleNozzleGradeTests`, 4, red controls asserted red inside each):
- one row in both modes (RED: today's two rows and two values);
- Stepped makes bands, plus the slicer line (RED: Stepped ignored);
- Manual: graded estimate layer by layer (RED: grade not in the sim, the estimate stays 1.69 mm);
- Auto: the grade in the sim, job bytes unchanged (RED: the grade written as the nozzle setting changes the job).

Branch `claude/flexible-screens` (PR #362). NOT pushed. Not installed (the installer does that). App only; core untouched; no

- **A face's card**: "Deepest squish [box]" becomes one read-only line, "Squishes ≈ 2.8 mm at 5 lb" — the app's estimate from
  your lattice, your weight and your stamp. Before the lattice is built it says "Squish estimate · Save & Exit to see it"; while
  the sim runs, "Squish estimate · working it out…". The curve-point box is gone.

  Twist stay yours. The chip on its wedge is a label. Lines about core's design ("core is designing it", "Can't reach on 13
  columns", "twisted 36% off") are not shown; a press that cannot be in the lattice at all (no stack, shared surface…) still says so.
- **The curve window** ([2D]/[3D]) opens as "Face 3 · what your lattice does": the estimated dent drawn in the same charts (its two

  does · deepest ≈ 2.8 mm", and one [Done] button. Nothing is written.

### How the estimate is made
The same sim the views use (the group's FE squish sim, solved on your lattice at its own stiffness, no core depth to scale it to).
A face's number is its deepest column's squish along its push; an edge's, the same on its press stack. Twice the weight gives
twice the squish; a firmer lattice gives less (your pad, Face 5: 15 % → 7.3 mm, 30 % → 1.3 mm, 30 % at twice the weight → 2.6 mm).

  own rule, the app's copy of it — FlexibleGroupField.assemble), then lays your densities on it. M1 used core's designed field for
  the owners; the lattice drawn is the same mask with the same densities.
- A Stamp face is pushed only under its stamp (your weight ÷ the stamp's footprint); a Curves face evenly (the curves are not an
  input in Manual).
- The estimate is the full-weight number even when the picture is cut back so it never folds.
- The window's curves are cross-sections through the deepest point (a "deepest anywhere" curve read flat on your Face 3).

## ★ Round 7 · U21 batch H — your notes of 2026-10-21, Img3: the edge press's lattice joins the face lattice cleanly (2026-10-22) (side lane, after checkpoint 1 below)

Side branch `claude/flexible-screens-u21-side2` (to be cherry-picked onto `claude/flexible-screens`). NOT pushed (your HOLD).
NOT installed (the integrator installs). App only; core untouched; no #354/main file edited; no new hook. No CORE LIST item.
Judged on your pad of 10-21 (`round7/batch_u21/his_live_1021_pad`, Group 2 = Edge 12 + Edge 9), lattice built through the page.

Your note (Img3, 13.png): "Edges/corners don't look great".

### What you will see now
- Where an edge or corner press's lattice meets the face lattice (the flat prism's slanted face), the walls run on across the
  join. The shredded, speckled fringe along the slanted side is gone, at rest and at your mid-way pause (s 0.5).
- The press's finer, brighter cells still end at the flat prism, and the colours are unchanged: that is core's design.
- Evidence: `round7/batch_u21_h/h_his13_beside_before_after.png` (your 13.png beside before/after crops at s 0 and s 0.5);
  the full frames `h_after_front-left-close_s0.png` and `h_after_front-left-close_s50.png` (the before frames are the plan
  probe's, same camera).

### What was wrong (one sentence each)
- The app cuts a press's lattice at its flat prism's plane voxel by voxel (C1's clip), so the density jumps from the press's
  0.18–0.32 to the face lattice's 0.14 inside one 1.04 mm voxel, up to 4.66 cell-size steps at once. The lattice drew all of
  those steps inside that voxel, which shredded a 1–1.5 mm band. Along lines through the plane that was 0.215 thin fragments
  per mm, against 0.005 away from it.
- Found while looking at the first fix's frames: at the part's outer faces, the voxels the builder fills in carried a press's
  density but no owner, so they were treated as face lattice and smeared the join there.

### What changed (code)
- `FlexibleGroupField.pressSeam` (new): for every voxel within 2.5 voxels of a press's plane:
  - the other side's density, carried across the plane along the arrow;
  - the press side's share, by the plane's true position (a ramp of ±1 voxel, ½ on the plane).

  Density itself is never changed.
- `FlexibleLatticeBuilder.inputs(pressCuts:)` stores them as `FlexibleLatticeInputs.rhoAcross` / `pressSide`. The owner now
  follows density through the builder's two fills.
- `FlexibleStageModel` changes one call: it passes its press cuts.
- `FlexibleLatticeField.seamSheet` (Swift) and `flx_wall_seam` (Metal, the twin):
  - In a cell with a seam, each side draws its own gyroid from its own same-side interpolation, with its own density gradient.
  - The two sides meet across the plane on a smoothstep of the share, with the whole gradient.
  - Every other cell is drawn exactly as before.
- `FlexibleLatticePass` uploads the seam in the (ρ, mask) volume's spare channels (rgba32Float, `rmN.w = 1`). A lattice

### How (code)
- `FlexibleOverlayMesh.displacements(perVertex:)`, used on the Squish page only (`FlexibleSettingsSquish.columnDents`; the main
  page and the goldens unchanged). Every drawn part point takes `CornerGrid.dent(u, w, t)`: a bilinear blend of the squares' own
  corner means (`quadCorners`, across a split face's cut too), corners with no value dropped and the rest renormalised, the far-edge
  row included, times the ramp of the nearest column. The squares themselves are unchanged. Controls: `controlCornerBlend` (the
  old rule) and `controlFarEdgeGate` (only rampValue's nil-column gate put back).
- `FlexibleBendPose(faces:field:)`: `FaceBend.bend(at:)` for a point within a pitch (≥ 1 mm) of a pressed face's plane, over its
  grid ± half a pitch. In the face's plane past the squares, it keeps the edge's value up to 40 mm (a stamp partly off the face).
  In the 3D sim, `FlexibleFEField.sample`. Other points keep the nearest vertex. Built by `FlexibleSettingsSquish.poseFaces` and
  passed through `Shown` to the page's `bendPose`. Control: `controlNearestVertexPose`.
- `FlexibleStageModel+PressSim`:
  - `edgesSimOnStaleLattice` holds when the lattice is out of date but was built on the scene open now
    (`lattice.sceneKey == openedKey`) and `feBase` is that lattice.
  - `startPressSims` runs then too, after your drag ends. `pressSimWants` takes its targets from `liveDesignTarget` (core's
    current per-press design, settled) when the lattice is out of date, and the key hashes the targets' depths.
  - `FlexibleSettingsSquish.field` accepts the edges group's sim once it answers the current presses (`pressSimIsCurrent`).
    `startSims` lets an edges group through.
  - `edgePreview` draws the preview when there is no sim to show.
  - Controls: `controlEdgesStillWhenStale`, `controlStaleUsesOldTuned`, `controlEdgePreviewOff`.
- Words: `FlexibleRowCopy.settingsEdgesLastSaved` (43 characters). In `FlexibleRowCopy+Views`: `pressHeatLine(tuned:)`

### How (code)

  guide; the red button 24 pt left), `FlexibleCancelInPlace` (the Lattice page), the labels, and the model's asks
  (`faceRemoveAsk`, `pressRemoveAsk`, `resetAsk`, `fixRemoveAsk`, one at a time, dropped by a tap, a row pick or a tab change).

  cleared (`railReturn`); the page's Undo/Redo (`historyWillRestore` → `restoreRailAfterHistory`) opens them again when that step
  brought the members back; `playingGroup`'s first-group default untouched (your 10-14 rule).
- F12 / Reset all: `sealAfterReopen` keeps the delete's step open until the re-opened scene's own write has landed in it, then
  seals (the project would seal a change alone 400 ms after it; the change is re-announced every 150 ms meanwhile, at most 5 s).
  The carry itself needs core's re-opened scene (the new lattice sections are core's), so it cannot run inside the trash. No
  ProjectModel hook.
- `removeFace`: seals before, saves after.

### What you will see now, in plain words
- **The window fills 80 % of the screen**, centred, over the page (13" portrait: 826 × 1102 pt, was 620 × 588). In 2D the two
  charts share the height (427 pt each, was 170). In 3D the table fills the rest (610 × 942 pt, was 588 × 481).
- **A column on the right, like a legend:**
  - **Mirror** beside each chart, marked with that curve's colour dot: [Left → Right] copies the left half onto the right, and
    [Right → Left] does the reverse.
  - **Copy** between the two charts: [X → Y ↓] / [Y → X ↑] for a face, and [Across → Along] / [Along → Across] for an edge.
  - A button that would change nothing is greyed. For example, once a curve is symmetric, its Mirror buttons grey out.
  - A corner has one curve, so its window has no buttons.
- **In 3D** the same column names each curve ("X · head-on from Top", "Y · head-on from Front") above its Mirror buttons. Small
  **L / R** tags at each curve's ends show which half is "left" on the table.
- **The 3D table always fits.** It stays inside its view and clear of the gizmo at every 45° turn. Before, a tall table would
  have cut off the sides of the square.
- **Nothing is saved until OK.** The buttons change only what the window shows, just like dragging a point. [OK] keeps it as one
  undo step. [Cancel] leaves the face or edge exactly as it was.

### What was wrong (one sentence each)
- Buttons: the window had only the point-by-point editor; there was no way to copy a half or a whole curve.
- Size: the card was capped at 620 pt wide, each chart at 170 pt and the 3D table at 460 pt (measured 60 % × 43 % of 13" portrait).

### What changed (code)
- `FlexibleCurveMirror` (new, pure):
  - `mirrored(curve, side)` keeps the source half's points bit-exact and places their reflection (x → 1 − x) on the other half.
  - The middle point is yours if one sits within core's 0.01 gap of ½ (your y, moved to ½). Otherwise it takes core's own
    curve value at ½ (`pen_curve_values`).
  - Kept points within the gap of the middle are dropped.
  - `changes(...)` decides which buttons are greyed.
- `FlexibleStageModel.mirrorDraftCurve` / `copyDraftCurve` write the window's draft only. Each one bumps `curveDraft.resets`, which
  clears the tables' selected point (passed into `FlexibleCurveTable2D` / `FlexibleCurveTable3D` as `resetToken`).
- `FlexibleCurveWindowLayout`:
  - The card is 0.8 × (the reader's size + its safe-area insets), centred on the screen, zIndex 60 as before.
  - The 2D charts get at least 140 pt each and share the rest. The 3D table gets at least 240 pt and fills the rest.
  - `fitted(camera, size)`: in a table taller than it is wide, the vertical lens widens by height ÷ width, so the camera fits
    the square table by its width.
- The 3D legend under the table moved into the column (kept under the table for a corner, which has no column).
- New copy lines in `FlexibleRowCopy+Edges` (all ≤ 16 characters).

### What you will see now, in plain words
- **Expand is a "+"**, depth keeps its up/down arrow. Before, both were the same arrow turned 90°.
- **The same two icons sit in the Selections list**, beside "Depth mm" and "Expand mm", right over their boxes. So the box in the
  list and the handle on the part read as one thing.
- **The two handles never touch.** There is always at least 24 pt of clear space between them, counting each box's full 44 pt tap
  band. Each box sits on the side away from the other handle (in your Img6 view: `−3.0 mm [+]   [⇕] 9.0 mm`). A tap on one can no
  longer open the other. If no spot on screen gives 24 pt (the open list right beside the floor with the screen's edge on the
  other side, or the "+" pointing off the screen), the "+" handle is hidden rather than drawn closer; the list's Expand box
  holds the same number. While you are dragging the "+" it is never hidden, even off the screen.
- **Dragging the "+" outward always grows the expand.** In some views it used to shrink it.

### What was wrong (one sentence each)
- Icons: both discs used one SF arrow at two angles (`arrow.up.and.down` / `arrow.left.and.right`), and the list's captions were
  text only.
- Gap: the discs were kept 72 pt apart centre to centre, but each box was always drawn to the right of its disc, with the expand
  handle on top. In 28 of 48 views of your l-bracket a disc lay under the other handle's box, and a click on the depth disc opened
  the **Expand** keypad (reproduced, below). The layout also assumed a 92 pt box, so the discs were drawn 2–5 pt off.
- Drag: the expand drag took its direction from the disc *as drawn*. That disc had been pushed out, so the direction came out
  reversed in 17 of 48 views. When that direction was short, it fell back to plain left-right, which ignores which way the knob points.

### What changed (code)
- `FlexibleLatticeHandles.depthSymbol` / `expandSymbol` (`"arrow.up.and.down"` / `"plus"`) are the one source. The discs and the
  new `FlexibleHandleCaption` (the list's caption row in `FlexibleSelectionsList`) both read them.
- `FlexibleLatticeHandles.layout(floor:rawKnob:depthBox:expandBox:viewport:keepOut:)` is pure:
  - Each handle is one unit: the 44 pt disc, 8 pt, then its measured box width, 44 pt tall.
  - Each box goes on the side away from the other handle.
  - The expand disc is pushed along its own direction in 4 pt steps (at most 240 pt) until the units are ≥ 24 pt apart, on screen
    and off the open list.
  - If that fails, the boxes move first (both right, both left, swapped). Flipping the knob to the other side is the last resort.
- `FlexibleOnModelLayer` draws each unit as `[box][disc]` or `[disc][box]`, centred on its rect. It measures each box's real width
  for the next layout. The chip's keep-outs (`handleRects`) and `underList` use the same unit rects.
- `dragExpand` now takes its sign and direction from the TRUE knob → 10 mm out. The projection sets only the mm per point; when it
  is shorter than 30 pt, #354's 0.05 mm/pt applies, still along that direction.

## ★ Round 7 · X20b — your answers of 2026-10-20: edge Play at core's full depth, curves off the part, faces in the curve window, another group's face bends along (2026-10-20) (the step before U21 above)

Branch `claude/flexible-screens` (PR #362), on top of `597eca0c` (C1). NOT pushed (your HOLD). App only; core untouched; no
#354/main file edited. Judged on your 10-20 pad (`round7/batch_u1/his_live_1020`).

### What you will see now, in plain words
- **Edge Play shows core's full depth.** On your pad, Group 2 now squishes Edge 12 by **5.58 mm** and Edge 9 by **3.33 mm**. Those
  are core's own design depths. Before this it showed 2.68 mm and 2.98 mm. Play, Bend and Heat all show the same squish.
- How: each press is solved on its own and scaled to core's depth for that press, then the two are added together. The old
  one-number scaling could not give Edge 12 and Edge 9 different depths. The band and the ½ "no-fold" cut are gone for these presses.
- The only limit left is a true fold, where a cell of the part would turn inside out. If that ever cuts the squish, a chip says
  "Shown at N% of core's depth: deeper folds". On your pad it does not cut: the thinnest cell keeps 33% of its volume, so no chip.
- **No curves on the part any more**, for faces and for edges. When a press is selected, its **indent** shows on the part, the way
  a stamp shows its outline: one line where the dent starts (10%), one at half (50%), and a dashed line around the deepest zone
  (90%). You cannot drag it there. You edit curves only in the 2D / 3D window.
- **Faces use the same window.** A face's Shape row now reads `Shape [Curves | Stamp] [2D] [3D]`. 2D shows the X curve table above
  the Y curve table. 3D puts both curves on one table with the gizmo (Top shows X head-on, Front shows Y head-on). OK keeps the edit
  as one undo step. Cancel puts it back.
- **Another group's face now bends along.** If a face from another group lies over the lattice being squished, it moves with it.
  On your 0004 split, with Face 3 playing, Top A moves 1.08 mm and Top B 0.54 mm (both were 0 before). A face that is not over the
  lattice stays still. (The 3D sim already moved everything; this was the column preview.)

### How (code)
- `FlexibleFERequest.solve`: for an edges group core designed, `Sim.perPress` solves one press at a time
  (`solveRaw`). `FlexibleFEField.designDepth(parts:targets:)` sets each kᵢ so the press's deepest compression along its arrow on
  core's press stack equals core's deepest design depth. It refines over 6 rounds so a neighbour's push is counted, then applies
  the true-fold guard (`foldFreeScale`, det(I+∇u) ≥ `FlexibleFE.trueFoldDet` 0.1). Targets are core's design
  (`designedSnap.buildableDepthMM`), not the press as built (C1's reviewer question 2). `FlexiblePressHeat.shownScale` is ×1 for
  such a field; the Squish page uses it too.
- `FlexibleIndent` (new): contour lines from data the app already has. For a face that is core's `liveS`, on the column grid. For
  an edge or corner it is the drawn push samples (`FlexiblePressPush.samples`). Shown by `FlexibleIndentLayer`, which takes no
  touches. The on-part editors stay only behind the red control `FlexibleIndent.controlCurvesOnPart`.
- `FlexiblePressCurveDraft.face`, `openFaceCurveModal`, `faceTables2D` / `faceCurves3D`. The face's X curve is keyed `.along` and
  its Y curve `.across`, the same storage as a press's curveX / curveY. `FlexibleCurveModalButton` is shared by both rows.
- `FlexibleOverlayMesh.addRiders` (+ `rampValue`): other loaded faces' column quads ride each dented face's ramp where they lie
  over its stack (`FlexibleSettingsSquish.columnDents`). Red control: `controlOtherGroupStill`.

## ★ Round 7 · R7-E2 PARKED — edge and corner presses are the shape only; nothing about them goes to core until the back-end phase (2026-10-19) (read this first)

Branch `claude/flexible-screens` (PR #362), on top of `c77b19fb` (R7-E1b). NOT pushed. App only; core untouched; no #354/main file
edited. His words (2026-10-19): "Please finalize the sending edges to core as soon as possible - as we are more focussed on the
front-end now. The back-end will come AFTER we have implemented the actual process."

### What you will see now, in plain words
- An edge or corner press is **the shape only**: the flat prism, its arrow (dashed), its handles, Deepest squish / Twist / Tilt and
  their limits all work as in E1b. Each press card says one grey line: **"Shape only · core support comes later"**.
- **Nothing about a press reaches core**: core does not design it, Auto does not weigh it, the lattice ignores it, and no job or
  export writes it. So the diagonal dense band across the part is gone, and your face groups' squish is what it was before E2.
  On your pad with Edge 14 + Edge 16 the lattice is bit-identical to E1's (53,248 voxels, 0 differ).
- His line was 45 characters (his rule is 44), so it reads "Shape only · core support comes later". "Shape only" already
  means "for now".

### How (one switch)
`FlexibleBackend.sendsPresses` (new `FlexibleBackend.swift`, **off**). When it is off: FlexiblePressSupport's gate keeps every
press out with `.backendLater`, so `sentPresses` is empty (the run job, the export's sends, the readiness, the hold and the
lattice's press fields all read it). `pressDesignTargets` is empty, so core is asked for no press design, press conflicts or Auto
request. `designInputs` strips the presses, which is E1's lattice key. The card shows the line as a plain caption (`warn` false).
Kept for the front-end: `registerPresses`, which reads core's stack for the limits and the halfway arrow, as in E1. Turning it on
gives back R7-E2 exactly as built.

   ≤ 44; RED: switch on → in the job) and `testHisPadsEdgePressesReachNoRequestToCore` (his pad with his live lattice + an edges
   group of Edge 16 + Edge 18: not sent, not designed by core, not in the lattice's key, no press design held; every send's job
   has no `press_direction` / `face_region_ids` and is byte-identical to E1's rule (presses stripped); both cards say the line;

  another edges group, taking that group's squeeze (one undo step). Shown only with two or more edges groups.

  ends". You can always go back up to that value. Fixes when there is one: [Deepen to N mm] (a twist whose short end hit 0 mm) and

### What you will see now, in plain words
- **An edge or corner press now goes to core.** Once core takes it (it stacks it, designs it, and nothing else is in its way), its
  arrow on the Squish page turns SOLID (it was dashed: "not sent yet"). While it is not in the job the arrow stays dashed and the
  card says why in one line.

  ("Twist stops at 7° · lattice ends") AND under it the press's own line, the first that applies: not in the job and why ("Set up ·
  core support pending" only while core's side cannot take presses at all; "Set up · core is designing it" for the second it takes;
  "Edge 16 and Face 3 share 85 mm²" with its fixes …) › a twist core cannot follow closely ("Twisted · squish shape up to 16% off",
  orange) › core's side label ("Side press · gyroid only · estimate", a plain grey caption).
- **The lattice under an edge press is core's design along its arrow.** The main Lattice page's lattice under Edge 16 is core's
  field over the press, blended into the faces' lattices by core's rule (the firmer wins between groups). On your pad this is a
  DENSE band right across the pad — see "A finding" below: core's press column runs through the whole part.
- **One group per export, said first.** With your Top group and an edges group both ready, the Lattice button's card says "core
  runs one squeeze group at a time" and offers [Send Group 1 only] [Send Group 2 only]. The faces' send carries no edge press;
  the edges group's send carries every edge press and rests the faces. With only the edges group, step ② reads e.g.
  "Group 1 · 11 lb · 2 edges · bead 0.45 mm".
- **Angled presses are estimates, said once.** The first time a side press goes into the job one line pops: "Angled presses are
  estimates until measured"; the Export caption says the same under core's line (the ruling's whole sentence behind its (i)),
  and About Flexible… lists it.
- **A twist says how close core gets.** Core has no "flat cut" map (you said not to ask for it), so a twisted edge is sent as the
  closest map core has; the card says how far off it is, from core's own columns: your Edge 16 twisted (typed 15°, the lattice lands
  it at 7°) is "up to 16% off"; untwisted it is 0.5 % and nothing is said.
- **Two presses can never share surface.** If a face is pressed whole while an edge press's piece lies on it, the edge press is
  kept out of the job with "Edge 16 and Face 3 share 85 mm²" and up to three fixes, the gentlest first ([Shallower] when it helps,
  [Face 3 rests], [Remove Edge 16]); core's own refusal of the same reads the same.

### A finding (core's verdict, nothing changed — the reviewer is asked)
On your pad an edge press's column, as core builds it (`build_press_stack`), runs from the press's surface to the far side of
the part: Edge 14 / Edge 16 at 45° are **52 columns of 136.5–140.1 mm** (the pad's diagonal), every one **too soft** for 5 kg
over that length, so core designs them at its densest buildable density (**ρ 0.362**) over **4,082 voxels** each. The lattice
under the edges group is therefore a dense band crossing the pad diagonally — with both edges, an X (`look/C01`, `C03`–`C07`).
The built lattice is exactly core's: 0 voxels differ from firmer(core's Top field, core's edges-group field). Whether that is
what should show, or a core need (a press column bounded, e.g. to the prism's depth), is question 1. #361 was not asked
anything (your 2026-10-18 answer).

### Why, and where this differs from the design (judge:final, R7-E2)
- **Core's map modes, not a "flat cut" (your answer: do not ask #361 yet).** Core's squish map has only both = X·Y, either and
  centre_edge. An untwisted edge is sent as "both": the axis along the edge at 1, the axis across a tent of 16 straight points a
  side peaking at the edge's own coordinate (core's to_uvt of the edge's ends) — core's curve rounds only the two segments beside
  the peak. Which of core's X / Y is "across" is read from core's frame, never assumed: on your 20 mm Edge 16, core's X is along
  the edge below 10 mm deep and across it above (the footprint is 20 mm long and 2h wide). A corner is centre_edge, straight.
- **A tipped corner stays centre_edge** (the design said "the closest product, X ramp × Y tent"): over a triangle a product of
  two curves is a poorer fit than core's edge-distance roof; its line says how far off it is, from core's columns.
- **"How far off" counts both ways** (|S·h − δ|, not only where core squishes more than the flat prism).
- **The twist's line comes before the side label** (the design had the side label first): on your pad every edge press is a side
  press (more than 15° off build Z), so the twist's honest line would never show; the side label shows when there is no twist.
- **The pop-up is one line** ("Angled presses are estimates until measured", ≤ 44 — your rule); the ruling's whole sentence is on
  About Flexible… and behind the Export caption's (i).
- **A press left out of a send is left out, never rested.** "Send Group 1 only" carries no edge press: core takes a press only as
  a loaded entry (a resting entry names one region), so the edges group's presses are simply not in that job — said behind the
  (i).
- **loadedKeys stays the faces'.** The design had the pipeline iterate "faces + registered presses" through loadedKeys; 100+
  readers take loadedKeys as faces (the dent, the walls, readiness, the settle waits), so the presses are designed beside them
  through their own list, with their own catch per press.
- **No FlexFaceGeometry for a press key yet**: nothing draws on a press's frame in E2 (its heat, bend and curves are E3/E4).
- **A tilted single-face press (AP1) is not sent** (no flat prism; never registered) and stays out of the lattice's key, so its
  bytes and the goldens' do not move.

### Why, and where this differs from what the verifiers suggested
- **The lattice stop's measurement (the bridge, ours).** Each press column's lattice run is measured on core's own samples and core's
  own lattice. At Balanced core leaves your Top's surface layer empty (its centres sit 0.31 mm above the part), so every column
  entering through the Top read "no lattice". The verifier suggested allowing about one voxel at the entry. Looking at the binding
  column showed a second effect: core also leaves voxels along the Top's triangle diagonal empty INSIDE the lattice at Balanced (a
  column entering at (3.6, 2.0, 20) has 1.56 mm of lattice, a ~1.5 mm hole, then lattice again). So the rule is: an empty stretch
  within two voxels of the entry is travel, and a hole no longer than one voxel's diagonal inside the run is crossed; a longer gap
  (the 50 mm between your Face 3 and Face 5 slabs) still ends it. Where a run has no hole (Fast, Fine, the sides) it is E1's, sample
  for sample. The diagonal hole is core's own voxelization; the reviewer is told (not asked of #361).
- **Two prisms on one face are HELD, not refused.** The verifier suggested refusing. Your typed values are held to every other limit
  (and the hold said), so this one is too; the plan still refuses anything that would leave a face group's face with no piece.
- **"Keeps some of itself" is 0.5 mm beyond every cut**, so between two prisms on one face at least 1 mm stays.
- **The angle stop is found by halving** (five halvings, each core's exact check on the cut it would make, nothing stored, about a
  second on your live project) and the best one is stored without opening the scene again.
- **The sawtooth fix touches only a pressed region whose squares DO step past its face's edge** (a turned frame — the corner's
  rest): its squares are kept inside the face's outer edge and behind the region's own cut lines, and a band one square wide of the
  region's own surface lies under them along both (dented like the rest of the part, in the colour of the square over it), so
  nothing steps out and no notch or colour step opens. Every other region, and a whole face, draws exactly as before (the first
  version banded every region with cuts and the suite caught it — below).

### Defaults taken (told to you, not asked)
- A new pick starts 3 mm deep (a face's default deepest squish).
- The flat prism only squishes the lattice the face-prisms make; it makes no lattice of its own.

- The Squish page's depth chip is tap-to-type for faces too.
- Edges and corners appear on the Squish page only.
- A twisted cut presses only the picked faces (the end face is not a member).
- "Keeps some of itself" = at least 0.5 mm of the face left beyond the cut.
- The named end of a twist: the top end of a steep edge; else the right (+X) or back (+Y) end (the gizmo's words).

### Why, and what is different from the plan
- **One plane, cut in each face.** The plane is P = {p : dot(p − A, d) = h}: d the arrow (the press's direction, core's
  press_direction, stored bit for bit), h the deepest squish, A the edge's deep end (its start when untwisted) or the corner. Each
  face's cut is the line P ∩ face, laid IN the face (not a 3D plane): core tests a region's cuts at voxel centres, and a 3D cut
  would move each face's boundary by up to half a voxel (the test shows 0.22–1.0 mm at core's 0.94 mm voxels on the cube).
- **The halfway is the whole faces'.** It is core's halfway over the whole member faces at pick time, stored on the press's area,
  and never re-aimed from the cut pieces (else the arrow would depend on the cut that depends on the arrow). On your pad's Top +
  Face 2 edge the two differ by one bit (printed), which the old engine would have moved.
- **The lattice stop reads the lattice the column STARTS in.** Core's lattice_mm counts every latticed bit of a column. On your
  live pad Edge 16's diagonal columns also cross Face 5's prism at the far side, so core's number alone would allow about 68 mm.
  The bridge now also returns, for a press's columns only, the latticed run from each column's entry — core's own quarter-voxel
  samples against core's mask, stopped at the first one outside the lattice — and the stop uses that. This is a measurement on
  core's columns and core's mask, not a frame, column or design of ours. **It is a judgment call; the reviewer is asked.**
- **The read-through is an accessor, not a rewrite at open.** The plan put it in FlexibleSettingsMigration.migrated (clearing the
  width at once). The M2 migration test pins its strips "bit for bit", so a strip saved with a width keeps its old half-spaces until
  you next change that press; every reader asks one accessor for its depth (FlexibleFlatPrism.depth(of:)).
- **His rule replaces the half-face rule** in every limit: a face only has to keep 0.5 mm of itself.
- **D-AP-13** (the camera down the arrow) is built as ruled. Looking down the arrow the head and the tail meet, so the knob is drawn
  56 pt (or more, clear of the chip) from the head along the edge's screen direction. The reviewer was asked to amend it.

### What you will see now, in plain words
- **With Finish None, the Top over each pocket is open, at Fast, Balanced and Fine.** The lattice runs right up to the top

- **Covered, Rim and Skin keep their look.** Covered is still a solid skin over the pockets. Rim still has its 2 mm solid
  band along the Top's edge, and now its middle opens. Skin still has solid between the holes, and now the holes go all the
  way through. Before, at Balanced, the sheet closed the Rim's middle and the Skin's holes too.
- **Fast and Fine look exactly as before.** Nothing in them changes (checked byte for byte on your pad).
- **A tap on the Top over a pocket** now reads the lattice there, not "solid here" (by the code: the tap reads "solid" only
  outside the lattice region; not tested here).

- **Bending**: what you see over the pockets is now the lattice itself, and the lattice moves with the squish once it is
  built (the main page, and the Squish page once the lattice is current). There is no lid left that the sim ignores. This
  was not re-tested in this step. The Squish page's quick preview before the lattice is built still moves only the pressed
  face; that is question 2 below.

**Why it happened, in one sentence:** at Balanced your 20 mm pad is 19.2 of core's 1.04 mm cubes tall, core drops the top
row of cubes because its centre sits above the part, and the app drew the leftover 0.2 mm between that row and the real top
as solid.

The pictures (`round7/batch_tl/look/`, offscreen frames by the shipping renderer, not device screenshots): your pad at
Balanced, Finish None, Heat off, from img_top_3's angle (matched by eye: azimuth 45°, elevation 0.62 rad), before and after,
at 900 and 1600 px, plus close-ups and the X-ray pair. "Before" is today's mask, built from the same core field.

### Why, in a little more detail
- Core voxelizes the part from its bounding box's corner, 96 cubes along the longest side at Balanced (1.0417 mm each). It
  keeps a cube only when the part encloses the cube's centre (voxelize.cpp's +Z winding rule).
- Your pad is 100 × 100 × 20. That is 96 × 96 × 19.2 cubes, so core makes 20 layers, and the top layer's centre is at
  z = 20.31, above the part. That layer is Empty.
- The app reads the lattice region from core's mask, smoothly between cube centres. The region therefore ended halfway
  between the last kept layer (z = 19.27) and the dropped one: at z = 19.79.
- With Finish None, the printed view draws as solid everything inside the part and outside the region. So the band from
  19.79 to 20 was drawn as a solid sheet over each pocket, and the walls stopped at 19.79.
- At Fast (64) and Fine (128) the top layer's centre is inside the part (19.53 and 19.92), so there was no sheet.
- The same gap could appear on any face of any part whose last cube centre falls outside it (on a tilted or curved face, as
  patches up to half a cube thick).

### The fix
- `FlexibleLatticeBuilder.inputs`: each cube core left Empty that touches a lattice cube face-to-face now joins the lattice
  region, with that neighbour's density. Those cubes lie outside the part, where the part's own surface cuts everything off,
  so the region simply runs out past the surface, as it already did at the sides.
- "Outside" means core's own rule (`coreEncloses`: the same arithmetic as voxelize.cpp, in the app). **This differs from the
  plan**, which said "the app's SDF > 0". The SDF version went red on Fine (T2). The app's distance field is made from
  voxels, and near an edge it reads part of the outermost voxel as outside. It called four cubes under the Top's edge
  "outside" although core had kept them, so the region would have grown sideways there.
- The density of each added cube copies its neighbour's, so the legend's range does not move.
- The (i) skips cubes whose centre is outside the part (the app's distance field), as the plan asked.
- Nothing else reads the mask: the squish sims read density only at core's own lattice cubes, so their requests are the
  same. `overLattice` (which part of the body is left open in the printed view) only gets firmer: on your pad 12 of 36
  vertices gained, none lost.

### ★ STOPPED on condition (d): "Lattice" on a new face waits for the reviewer
The reviewer's condition (d) said a lattice-only group is OK "ONLY IF it changes nothing about a Topology run … if it does
change a Topology run, STOP and tell the reviewer". I measured it before writing any code, on your pad
(`round7/batch_d2/conditionD/`): a new group holding Face 4 with only a lattice role (no anchor, load or Protect).
- **Without H35** its lattice role is dropped (#354's rule), the group is "Pending", and **Topology's Optimize is blocked**
  ("finish the pending group"). The Topology job is unchanged.
- **With H35** Optimize is allowed and nothing is anchored, loaded or protected, **but Topology's job is not the same**: its
  lattice block gains Face 4's slab (3 479 → 4 374 bytes). Every face-prism of a Flexible project already rides Topology's
  lattice block today (your Group C's do); this would be one more.
So **H35 is not landed**, and on the new-face chip **[▦ Lattice] is greyed** with one line: "Lattice on a new face waits for
a review". Everything else on the chip works. To get a lattice face now: **"Add to Group C as lattice"** (when a group was
picked first), or **Protect** and then **▦ Lattice** on the face's chip (two taps). Posted to the reviewer with three options
(comms 2026-10-18T02-40-59.241Z-362-7436ed); my recommendation is (A): land H35 and accept the face-prism in Topology's
lattice block, as every other face-prism is. Nothing writes `latticeOnlyGroups` meanwhile (the field exists, optional,
never encoded while empty — old projects open; tested).

  half the scrubber and its line were hidden. Now:

  below it.

  - At 11" landscape the tall Preview card now scrolls a little: 306 of its 412 pt show, and Export is a short scroll away.

  (+Z −Z +X / −X +Y −Y, 48 pt tall). The current direction is lit.

  - A tap goes back to the rows.

    says gravity is −Z. Topology keeps its own panel, unchanged.

  - ② says "Core runs one squeeze group at a time" on ONE line. Its (i) moved under the word "Core".

### What you will see now, in plain words

**On the Squish page**
- **A face's own weight is shared equally between its lattice parts** (your answer 7: "5 lb each of 10 lb"). Face 4 and
  Face 2 at your 10 lb now press 10 lb each in all: 5 lb on each of their two parts. Before this fix each PART pressed
  10 lb, so each face pressed 20 lb and Group 2 pressed 40 lb, while its box still said "Squeeze 10 lb". The box still says
  10 lb; each part's row says 5 lb. (The Top, linked to the main page, was already right: 11 + 11 of 22 lb.)
- **The parts of one face go together.** A group chip or "+ New" on one part moves the whole face; the Squeeze box gives
  each face its force, shared by its parts; taking one part out (⊖) puts the face's whole force on the part that is left.
- **The face card's group chips show the names on your pad** — on their own line under "Squeeze group" when they don't fit
  beside it. With your three groups they had always fallen back to one "● Group 2 ⌄" menu.
- **With Bend on, everything goes to the full bend** (your answer 1 of 2026-10-15): the depth chip ("↓ 22.5 mm") and the
  Prisms view's depth labels move with the bend now, and so do the prisms' floors.
- **Bend always shows the open group's own bend.** The page kept the first bend it drew in a session (two groups' bends
  looked the same to its memory), so with Bend on, switching groups or editing a curve could leave the curves, stamp and
  prisms at the wrong pose. This was also why one of F's tests failed only when other tests ran before it.
- The rail counts **faces** ("Group 2 · 2 faces", not 4), and the pinch line names the face whole ("Pinched with Face 2 ·
  two halves", not "Face 2 · lattic…").
- "Violet = lattice · tap to pick" shows only while something on the part IS violet.
- The take-out ⊖, [Delete], [Keep], [Reset all] and [Reset] are 44 pt targets now (drawn as before; the ⊖ a little
  darker so it reads beside "Rests").
- "Delete Group 3?" no longer stays up for a group that has gone, or when you open another tab (a new group reusing the
  number could have been deleted by it).
- After Reset all, Heat no longer wears the "every group" mark with no group left.

**On the main Lattice page**
- **After Reset all and an empty Exit, the pill says "Lattice · Nothing to squish yet"** (your answer 3 of 2026-10-15), in
  the neutral style — no orange "Fix: press the face that carries weight". A tap opens the Squish page (it still never
  opens by itself). The heat icon is dimmed: there is nothing to heat.
- **A tap on a face's solid middle picks the group of that face's lattice parts** (it kept the last group, with no cue).
- **Heat starts on the first group every session** (your answer 2 — already so; now pinned by a test).
- Not changed yet: after the empty Exit the main page shows the plain pad (question 1 below).
- When the redesign lands (not yet true): "On the Flexible screen you can't move a Topology piece by tapping it."

### The spike: how the solid part is cut open over the lattice (the go / no-go, posted to the reviewer)
- **The plan's solid-flag route alone is NO-GO.** It draws the body see-through with its closed surface flagged opaque. #354's
  see-through body writes no depth, so whichever triangle is drawn last wins: on your pad the far side face painted over the
  Top (`spike/R7X1_spike_a_solidflag_alpha0_img1.png`, `_top.png`). The plan's "body alpha just below 1" cannot work either:
  the open surface would be ~opaque (`spike/R7X1_spike_a_solidflag_alpha0998_img1.png`).
- **GO, still hook-free:** the same flags, PLUS the closed body written into the G-buffer by OUR pass (new `flx_body_vertex` /
  `flx_body_gbuffer`, eye-Z pushed 0.5 mm back). #354's shade then writes its depth into the main buffer, so the see-through
  body drawn after it keeps only its nearest closed surface; the walls are marched against the same buffer, so a wall behind
  the closed body is never drawn (`spike/R7X1_spike_b_printed_bodyInGBuffer_img1.png`, `_top.png`). The pass is fed through
  the existing map-depth hook (it notes the renderer's buffers; no new hook). Taps still pick the face under them (by
  construction: the pick pass draws the unchanged body mesh — not measured by a click here).
- **The printed term in both twins** (MSL `flx_field` under the reserved `shape2.w`; Swift
  `FlexibleLatticeField.lattice(at:printed:)`): S = max(dPart, min(max(dRegion, −dSkin), −dRegion)), field = min(F, S).
  **One extension to the plan's term** min(F, max(dRegion, dPart, −dSkin)): the part OUTSIDE the region (−dRegion) is solid
  too — the pocket's own wall and floor. Without it a ray through the voids ran on through your pad's solid middle to the
  other strip. The march's early-out bound is min(max(dRegion, dPart, dSkin), S) in the printed view (both bounds hold).
- **AO check** (the plan's): the solid part next to the strips against #354's opaque body, mean ΔE 0.00 (img5 top, 900 and
  2064 px) and 0.05 (img1) — no crease loss: the printed body's occlusion comes from the G-buffer (body and walls together).
- **At your 13" pixel size** (2064 px, the G-buffer capped at 1152 below it) the body's edges stay crisp (it is still drawn
  full-size, multisampled); only the walls are at the G-buffer's size, as before.

### What you will see, in plain words

**On the Squish page**
- **A group's trash asks first.** Tapping it puts one line in the panel's header: **"Delete Group 2? · [Delete] [Keep]"**
  (your name for the group if you gave one: "Delete Thumbs?"). Only [Delete] deletes it, and one Undo brings it back.
- **A face row's trash is now a small ⊖ (take out)**, smaller than the group's trash. It still takes only that face out.
- **After Reset all you can leave with nothing set.** Exit reads "Save & Exit" (or "Exit" if nothing changed), never
  "Fix 1 thing". The top line says **"Nothing to squish yet"**. It names no face (it no longer suggests the Top), has no
  [Fix], and no pop-up opens on any tab.
- **Tapping the Top after Reset all** starts Group 1 on the lattice part under your tap, at an **equal share** of the main
  page's Top weight: 5 of 10 kg (11 of 22 lb) for each of the two lattice parts. Tapping the other part adds it at the other
  half. M2 had already built this; the new test only confirms it.
- **The face card's group chips show the names** ("Thumbs", "Group 2", "Group 3", "+ New"). They are squeeze-group names
  only: the main page never shows them.
- **With no view on you see only the curve**, with no colour. The page now opens with Heat off. Heat on shows the open
  group's colour, and a 3 s hold shows every group's. Bend shows the bend, and Play plays the sim.
- **Bend and Play are never on together.** Turning one on turns the other off, on both pages (the views are shared).
- **With Bend on, everything drawn on the part sits where the bent part puts it:** the curves, the stamp and its handle,
  the group discs and outlines, the prisms' faces and the glass. What stands *inside* the part stays put: a prism's floor,
  its depth chip and the Prisms view's floor tags. The bent face comes down to meet them. Bend alone no longer hides the
  curves and chip. The body is still drawn solid so the bent part reads.

**On the main Lattice page**
- **The heat follows the squeeze group of the face you last tapped**, and the first group until you tap one. A **3 s hold on
  the heat icon shows every group's** heat (the icon fills and wears your groups' three colours). A tap hides the heat;
  the next tap shows the selected group's again.
- **The play bar has no group picker any more.** What plays is the same selected group, and every group in turn under the
  hold. "Play all" used to be the default with two groups; it is now the hold.

Your live lattice (Group C = Face 3 + Face 5, Lattice at 25 mm) leaves the Top with lattice only in two 25 mm strips — one
under each face-prism — and solid between them. Faces 0, 2 and 4 the same: a 25 mm lattice band at each end.

- **A tap on the Top near Face 3 picks "Face 1 · lattice B"** — the 25 × 100 mm part of the Top that has lattice under it. Its
  curves run along that part only (100 mm one way, 25 mm the other), its depth prism and its dent stand on it only, and the
  solid middle never moves. (Before: the tap picked the whole Top and the curves ran 100 mm across the model — the red-control
  picture.)
- **A tap on the solid middle picks nothing.** One line appears under the top line: **"Solid here · only face-prisms get
  latticed"** with one button, **[Go to Lattice]**, which leaves the Squish page for the main Lattice page (where face-prisms are
  set). Your edits are kept; nothing is baked.
- **The Top's 22 lb presses both lattice parts, 11 lb each** — your answer 7 ("an equal share per lattice part … whatever their
  size"). With Face 5's face-prism at 10 mm the parts are 25 and 10 mm wide: still 11 + 11.
- **A face you pressed whole before you set the face-prisms now presses its lattice parts** (your pad: the Top, Faces 2 and 4).
  Each part takes the face's settings (group, curves, deepest squish, weight link). A stamp stays stored where you drew it, but a
  part whose lattice does not hold the stamp's centre is set to Curves, and the page says so once: "Stamp on solid · the
  lattice part is Curves". The whole face is never left pressed beside its parts (core would refuse the job).
- **Where a tap works:** a lattice part nobody presses wears a faint violet; the legend card adds one row, "Violet = lattice ·
  tap to pick". The solid rest of the face stays the part's colour. Pressed parts show their heat as before.
- **A face wholly inside one face-prism (Faces 3 and 5) is the face itself** — its id, its card, its job bytes as before. Two
  face-prisms that together cover a face (your split top's halves) also leave it whole. A face with no lattice at all keeps its
  card ("No lattice under it").
- **A face-prism depth change keeps each lattice part and its curves** (the same part, the same id): Face 3 at 17.26 mm — the
  Top's part is 17.26 × 100 mm, your curve kept.
- **Edges and corners nest inside the lattice.** Edge 14 (Face 2 + Face 3 — on your live lattice it is numbered **Edge 16**: the
  list follows the lattice parts) takes a 12.5 mm strip inside Face 2's 25 mm band (half the band) and a strip on Face 3; the band
  keeps the rest. An edge whose lattice on a face lies in two places is refused ("Edge N · its lattice is in two places"); with a
  face-prism set, an edge on a face with no lattice is greyed ("No lattice at Edge N · set a face-prism").
- **What moved off the Surface stage:** the edge/corner STRIPS and their RESTS. Round 6 (I2) cut them into the Surface stage's
  own regions, so they showed on the Surface stage and in Selections' Regions popover, and Topology, the lattice stage and the
  Stress solve declared them in their jobs. Now they are Flexible-only: the Flexible stage never writes the Surface stage's
  regions; the strips live on their presses and are cut, every time, on a private copy. A project I2 saved is moved once when it
  opens — the Surface stage gets its regions back exactly as before the cut, the Flexible job declares the same strips (the same
  cuts, bit for bit) under new ids, and a toast says "Edge strips now live on Flexible only". If something was already undoable
  when the stage opened, the move rides your next Flexible edit instead (one undo step). **Your simulator's projects have no I2
  strips** (checked on a read-only copy): nothing moves for you.

### The blast radius, the fixtures and the re-pins (each attributed in the test)

**The blast radius (ruling 4's gate, counted before any fixture change).** The targeted suite ran with the gate on and the old
fixtures: chunks 1–2 (21 classes, 85 tests) gave 3 failures, each a test waiting out its 180–400 s timeout for a lattice that no
longer comes (the golden's C1 pad field, `FlexibleBatchM2Tests.testTheTwoPagesAgreeOnAFourFingertipStamp`,
`FlexibleBatchM2VerifyTests.testAWholeFaceRigidPlateFollowsTheMainPagesSim`). **I stopped that count there** (by PID, after 26
minutes): at that rate the 192 classes would have taken many hours of timeouts. The fixture change below was made instead, and
the full suite was run on it (run 1). Every failure of run 1 is listed in the table after this one, with its fix.

**Fixtures** (your real workflow: a face-prism under the pressed faces, through the shared builders):
- `FlexibleHisProject.padProject` (34 suites use C1's pad) sets, by default, a face-prism under the pad's top, 20 mm deep. That is

- **A name goes to the group you typed it on.** Suppose you tap Group 2's name, type "Thumbs", then tap Group 1's tab
  before pressing Return. Group 2 is now "Thumbs", Group 1 is unchanged, and Group 1's header has no open field.
- **The rail's tab shows the new name, or the new colour, as soon as you change it.**
- **Names are 12 characters at most. They are never cut on the rail.** A long name wraps onto two lines in its tab:
  "Index finger" fits on one line, and the widest 12 characters take two.
- **Reset all leaves only [Model] and [+ New], with no pop-up.** The top line still says what is missing, and Exit still
  reads "Fix 1 thing" (question 5 below asks whether an empty setup may leave). With today's rule, the
  "[Press Face 1]" pop-up would have put the Top back. It also turned the camera to the top view.
- **[+ New] does what its line says ("Tap the face that starts it") once faces are pressed.** A tap on a face that no
  group holds starts the next group. If no main-page group gives that face a weight, the keypad row
  "Face 3 → Group 4 [#]" asks for one. Your weight starts the group in one undo step, and its tab opens. Before, the
  tap opened Group 1. On [Model], a tap on such a face opens the group you were last working on, where the face's card
  offers [Press it].

- His rule: ONE visible line per setting, never cut.

#### Rulings and rules this batch reverses (his 2026-10-14 words win)
- **S5 (round 5): "Reset all = a brand-new setup with the main page's loads read in"** → nothing read in; only [Model] [New].
- **S8 (round 5): "the rail follows the selected face after every edit"** → the open tab is the master; only his picks move it
  (round 5's rule is the red control).
- **D2 / round 5: the × MERGES a group into another, shown only with two or more groups** → a trash on every group that
  DELETES it. ("Join the groups", the pop-up's fix, still merges — `mergeGroup`.)
- **R6 item 3: the Prisms view tags every pressed face** → only the open group's (the prisms themselves stay).
- **[+ New] hidden when nothing is pressed** → always shown.

#### Where I departed from the brief (and why)
1. **His pad already has three groups**, so the brief's "Group 2 = newGroup(with: 3), Group 3 = edges" is Group 4 = Edge 9
   here; the test runs every tab of the four.
2. **"Face 1's chip reads 3.0 mm"**: his saved pad's Face 1 is a 12 mm Stamp face; the 4g test first sets it to Curves,
   3 mm, as his img3 shows it, then checks "3.0 mm".
3. **noLatticeUnder does not stand on A1_0003 as saved**, so the 4f test makes it stand on Face 1's rest by setting core's
   latticed share to 10 % in the readiness inputs (nothing else changed).
4. **Names stay on the Settings page.** The main page's player picker and the "Group 2 would squish …" warning (the shared
   readiness, also the main page's pill) keep "Group N" — "nothing on the main page changes". Asked below.
5. **newGroup(with:) opens the new group only when made from the face he works on** (its card's [+ New] chip); a face
   moved to another group by its chips leaves the tab where it is (the face leaves its list).
6. **An edit never gains or moves a selection the code made elsewhere** (found by the suite: the main page's shared model
   gained a selection from an edit made on its page). Opening a tab still selects its first face.
7. **Reset's regions are compared by `regions`**: FaceRegionModel's id counter keeps advancing (ids are never reused), so
   the model differs only in that counter.
8. **The hosted tests run synchronously**: the page's Metal view publishes its projection only with the run loop pumped
   (an async hosted test drew no overlay at all, so its chip check would have been empty).

### Round 7 · batch R7-V — the views on both pages: icons only, Play, his pause holds, X-ray back, Settings' Heat and Bend (2026-10-14, with the verify's fixes)

Your 2026-10-14 breakdown, the views half (img1, img3, img4, img5), with your two sets of answers. Built hook-free: **no #354 or
main file was touched** (WorkspacePlaceholder, MetalMeshView, ProjectModel unchanged). **The app was not launched**; the pictures
are offscreen — the shipping renderer for the part, the pages' SwiftUI chrome hosted over it — not device screenshots, and the
camera is the probe's (your img1 / img5 views), not the page's own framing.

**What you will see — the main Flexible page:**
- **Icons only.** "Role colours off" and "Prism after a pick" are gone. Both behaviours are now fixed on: the model wears no
  Selections role colour, and a group's faint prism shows only after you pick the group in Selections (nothing on open, none
  for a Pending group).
- **No squish number on the main page** (your answer: "The squish number: only on the Squish page") — not after a pick, not
  under [Prisms]. Your img2 "12.0 mm" is gone. The face-prism's own number, tap-to-edit and equal to the list, is R7-M's.
- **Six view icons:** Heat · Stress · Lattice · Prisms · **X-ray** · **Play**. They sit on one line where the "Lattice ready"
  note still fits beside them; otherwise (11" portrait, the iPad mini) they wrap three over three.
- **Play is OFF when a project opens.** There is no play bar, and the model sits at rest. Heat keeps its full-load colours.
  Tap Play: the bar comes back and the squish plays. Play combines with every other view, and no other icon turns it off.
  While the sims run or refine, the Play icon carries a **turning blue arc** on its rim; when a sim failed (or its refine did
  not land) it carries an **orange dot** — turn Play on and the bar says why. (The bar's lines are hidden with the bar.)
- **Your pause holds — and the model stays where you paused it.** After you pause (❚❚, or a drag on the timeline), nothing
  restarts or moves the squish: not an edit, a rebuilt lattice, its sims landing, Save & Exit, a Stress retry, or a legend's
  reading ending; a new field binds at your paused amount. Only Play restarts it (▶, or the Play icon). Play off puts it at
  rest.
- **X-ray is its own icon again; its starting state follows your finish.** With **Covered**, X-ray starts OFF: the opaque
  model, which is the print (the skin hides the lattice). With **None, Rim or Skin**, X-ray starts ON, so your lattice shows —
  **your pad is saved with Finish None**, so it opens in X-ray, the lattice inside the ghost. This lasts until R7-X's printed
  view, which will show the lattice through the finish with X-ray off. Your tap on X-ray wins and is kept for the session
  (per project). X-ray off hides the walls under every finish for now.
- **The Lattice icon is lit while its walls are seen**, which means in X-ray for now (so it is lit as your None pad opens). Turning it on turns X-ray on too,
  following your rule "a view that needs another turns it on itself". [Prisms] also turns X-ray on, because a prism sits
  inside the part. Turning the lattice off leaves X-ray as you set it.

**What you will see — the Settings (squish) page:** three new icons under the gizmo, after [Prisms] [Groups]:
- **[Heat]** (the main page's thermometer).
  - It opens showing the **current group's** heat; the other groups' maps are uncoloured.
  - A **tap** hides the heat; another tap brings the current group's back. Hiding the heat also ends a legend reading, so a
    tap on the part selects again.
  - A **3-second hold** shows **every group's** heat — the icon then carries **three small dots in your groups' colours**, so
    "every group" is told from "this group" at a glance. Its release does not undo it. A tap then hides it.
  - **The added layer is gone:** no group glass is drawn over a face that shows heat. Glass appears only where heat is hidden.
  - The legend card's heat rows show only while heat shows.
- **[Bend]** (a compress glyph).
  - It shows the current group **at full depth, every face at once, frozen**. On your pad, Group 2's Face 4 and Face 2 pinch
    together, and with a current lattice the 3D sim moves the whole part.
  - **Bend alone** (Heat hidden, no Prisms or Groups, no Play) shows only the bent model — **opaque and shaded**, so the
    full-depth shape reads (it was a near-black ghost): no curve, chip, tag, prism or glass. With Heat, the heat colours the
    bent faces over the X-ray ghost, and the curves, chip, tags and prisms come back (they stand at the rest pose — open
    question 4). With the heat hidden and Prisms, Groups or Play, the body is at 30 %.
  - **With Play**, the bar animates and the full-depth pose shows as a faint ghost.
  - An edges/corners group says "No bend yet · core support pending".
- **[Play]**, the same Play view as the main page, shared: turning it on on one page turns it on on the other. With Play off
  there is no bar and the model sits at rest (your curve shows as colour only — turn on Bend to see the full dent). With Play
  on, the squish plays, your drawing too. Its icon carries the same blue arc (the 3D sim running) and orange dot (it failed).
  At 11" portrait the bar's line takes a shorter form when the long one would be cut ("Column preview").

  rendering anyways"): X-ray is its own icon again, and the Lattice view no longer IS the X-ray.

  longer turns X-ray on. It still decides whether the walls are a ghost under its solid planes *in* X-ray.
- **Batch V's two view settings** (your 2026-10-10 request, "Bring both back as a view setting that can each be turned off at
  will"): removed, with both behaviours fixed on. The settings are no longer kept per project in the app's defaults; your
  stale keys (`flexible.mainViewSettings.<id>`) are removed once, when a project opens.
- **Round 3's Settings "editing hold at full squish"** ("while he edits it holds still"): with Play on, the squish plays,
  your drawing too ("When it is on the simulation plays"). With Play off, the default, it sits at rest (your answer).
- **R6's Groups glass over the heat** (R6 review: each glass's alpha set over its own heat): no glass is drawn over a heated
  face now. The alpha rule still applies wherever heat is hidden.
- **S1b's main-page squish tags** (round 6 item 3, your img3 then: "we should automatically be able to see the amount of
  squish it has been set to"): reversed by your 2026-10-14 img2 and answer ("The squish number: only on the Squish page").

#### Decisions to flag (not asked, said here)
- The Heat view's bit is stored as **"heat hidden"** (`FlexibleStageViews.heatOff`, with `heatAll` for every group). That
  way the page opens with the current group's heat with no first-open flag, and FlexibleStageModel.swift is not edited
  (R7-S's file). The brief named the bits `.heat` / `.heatAll`; the behaviour is the same.
- **Play is shared session state** (`FlexibleStageViews.play`), never a setting: Exit stays "Exit".
- **The pause latch lives in the loop class** (`FlexibleSquishLoop.pausedByHim`), so the Settings page's own loop keeps your
  pause too. While paused, a new lattice or sequence starts where you left it: held there, cycle 0, the new field bound at once.
- **Play all while paused:** the group on screen is held, and a new lattice resets it to its first group (cycle 0).
- **(review) X-ray's starting state follows the finish** — a stopgap until R7-X's printed view, so your None pad never opens
  with its lattice hidden. The reviewer may rule otherwise (the verify offered three options); it is one property
  (`xrayDefault`).
- **(review) Your pause freezes the pose** (my open question 3, answered by your img1 words: "Only by pressing Play should the
  sim actually restart" — a model that moves after your pause reads as a restart).
- **(review) The squish number left the main page now**, not with R7-M: these batches are installed one by one, and the 12 mm
  would have stayed in front of you until R7-M. R7-M keeps its plan (face-prism chips, tap-to-edit).
- **(review) A test seam on the Settings page** (`FlexibleStagePage.testDrill`, a subject nothing in the app sends): the hosted
  harness's clicks land on the MTKView under the chrome (AppKit's hit test), so the legend's drill is driven through it.

## Round 6 · batch I2 — edges and corners as squeeze groups (your item 2, as you approved it) (2026-10-11)

The two group lists stay separate (your 2026-10-10 reversal, 7f710903): this batch works inside the Settings page's
squeeze groups only. **The main page's Selections are not touched** — no row added, renamed or regrouped; a strip cut
never joins a Selections group. **The app was NOT launched**: installed on the iPad Pro 13 simulator (147E56A1), never
opened. The pictures are offscreen (the shipping renderer for the part, the hosted panel beside it), not device
screenshots.

**What you will see (Settings page):**
- **[+ New] asks first, on one line: [Faces] [Edges/corners].** Faces is the list you know. Edges/corners opens a new
  group (its number after yours, the first colour no group wears) in pick mode.
- **Pick mode: every edge and corner of the part, highlighted and listed.** On your pad: 8 corners and 12 edges,
  numbered 1–20 by position — the same number on the part's tag and on its row. Each wears a colour from the eight group
  colours minus the new group's own, and two that touch (an edge and the corner at its end, two edges meeting) never wear
  the same one. A candidate facing away is drawn faint, untagged, and stays in the list.
- **Pick by the list or on the part.** A tap takes the nearest corner within 22 pt, else the nearest edge; tapping the
  same spot again steps to the next candidate there — at your img3 camera the end-on edge between Face 2 and Face 3
  (#14) sits under its two corners and is reached on the third tap. Every tag is a 44 pt target. Picked ones turn the
  group's colour, thicker, with ✓. In pick mode a tap never selects a face.
- **Grey, with one line why:** a face taken out of the setup ("Face 5 was taken out of the Flexible setup"), a candidate
  over another edges group's strip ("In Group 4"), core's refusal of the press, a fillet ("A fillet · strips need a
  sharp edge"), a curved edge. On your pad as saved, all 20 can be pressed (core was asked about each).
- **Before [Done], one line per face that is in a face group:** "Face 1 keeps the rest · strip for Edge 9". (Your faces
  read "Face 1" here, so the line takes its short form; with a short name it reads "Top keeps the rest · strip taken for
  Edge 3", ≤ 44 characters either way.) The card also carries the group's one squeeze force — a press never invents a
  weight; [Done] opens the keypad on it if it is empty.
- **[Done · N picked] is ONE edit and ONE undo step.** An edge presses a STRIP along it on each of its two faces; a
  corner a square PATCH on each face that meets there. Each is cut with the Surface stage's own cut. The face's own
  squeeze group **keeps the rest**: its settings (weight and its link, group, curves, stamp, deepest) move onto the rest,
  re-expressed through core's frames — your stamps stay exactly where you drew them on the part. Where two picked edges
  meet the first keeps the shared corner square; a corner takes its square out of the strips' ends; nothing overlaps.
- **The new group's tab:** "Group 4 · 1 edge" on the rail; its force; each press as one row — "Edge 9 · Face 1 + Face 2",
  its **Strip width** box (mm; tap to type, drag to scrub), "Set up · core support pending", and which faces keep the
  rest. The strips wear the group's glass on the part.
- **Strip width:** starts at the lattice depth under the faces (core's, the smaller of the two), never more than half
  the face across the edge, so the face group always keeps a rest. On your pad: Top 20 mm, Face 2 100 mm of lattice,
  Face 2 is 20 mm tall → 10 mm. A change re-cuts that strip and any that meet it — one undo step.
- **Each pick is a press at core's halfway, saved, never sent.** The arrow points halfway between the faces as CORE
  frames the strips (45.00° from each face on your pad's edge), in the new group, at the force you typed. Nothing of it
  is written to any job until core builds press stacks (AP9). The faces that gave a strip are their rests in the job now
  (below).

**A correction I owe you (batch N, the realistic fold).** I told you the tested squish curves make TPU
lattice stiffen as its cells close. For your filament they do not. varioShore gyroid at 240 °C SOFTENS
between its tested points: the secant falls 24 % from 10 % to 25 % squish at ρ 0.15. The stepped solve's
stiffening comes from a textbook densification law (Gibson & Ashby), joined smoothly past the data's end
(25 %). And 34–38 % of your pad's two groups is squeezed past that point. Without that law, the stepped
field folds MORE than the linear one (your Group 1: 91 inverted cells against 24). So "folds realistically"
rests on an untested extrapolation. Core brief #40 asks for curves tested up to densification. See
"Round 5 · batch N — a squish that folds realistically" below, section "The curves (the premise,
corrected)".

**What N gives on your pad:** Group 1 at full size has 0 inverted cells (the linear sim, uncut, had 24),
so the fold cut is no longer applied. Group 2 is the same. It takes about 16 s per group on this Mac,
after the quick squish. Still open: Group 1 plays at 2× your weights (the band edge, your call). Its top
edge rises about 8 mm, and some lattice walls under that ridge look shattered with the heat view off.
Both need core's large-deformation solver (#36) and per-voxel ν (#41).

## Round 5 · batch N — verification pass

Batch N's verifier found ten things. Each is confirmed below with my own run (not the verifier's word),
fixed where the app can fix it, and pinned by a test with a RED control computed beside it. **The app was
NOT launched: nothing here has been seen on a device or simulator.** Pictures are offscreen frames of the
shipping renderer.

**What changes for you on the main Flexible page:**
- **The refined squish is closer to right.** A refine used to stop on a damped step that said "settled"
  while the field was still 7 % (1.5 mm) short. Now only an undamped step can stop it. Your Group 1 now
  stops 8 solves into its last increment. Eight more undamped solves from where it stops move it 0.32 mm
  (1.4 %); from the old stop they had moved it 1.5 mm (7 %). The refine takes 18.5 s in Release (it was
  16.7 s).
- **The note names the group and never blanks.** "Refining Group 1… 1/8" appears the moment the refine
  starts. It counts the increment being solved, so it shows 8/8 while the slowest step runs. Then
  "Refining Group 2… 1/8". Before, it went blank for 1.5 s, stalled on 7/8, then restarted at 1/8 unnamed.
- **Every note fits, whole, beside the Play-all picker at 11" portrait.** "Refine didn't settle" /
  "Refine took too long" / "Refine failed" replace "Quick squish · the refine did not settle", which was
  cut to "Quick squish · the refine did…". Batch G's two lines were cut there too. They now read
  "Squish sim failed" and "Group 2's sim failed".
- **Nothing changes mid-squeeze when the refined squish lands.** The legend's top, the colours and the (i)
  stay with the quick squish still playing. They change at the rest point, together with the shape. Your
  Group 1's legend top had jumped 23.72 → 20.98 mm mid-squeeze and recoloured the quick squish.
- **The (i) now says the force and the turns.** For your Group 1: "…finding this part 7× stiffer than core's
  columns (its skin and walls carry load), pressed at 2× your weights, with no buckling or self-contact, and
  big turns drawn as stretches (an edge it turns far rises) — tap here, then the part, for the mm there."
  Group 2 says "pressed at 1.6× your weights" and nothing about turns, because none of its elements grow.
- **A new lattice stops a refine within one solve.** It used to wait for the whole increment: up to 6
  solves, 6.5 s on your Group 1. A Stress solve waiting for core gets it within one solve too.

**What is still wrong, and it is the first thing you will see on Group 1** (`batch_n_verify/NV_his_g1_front_2x_vs_his_weights.png`):
- At full squeeze the whole Face 5 end **leans over** (about 30°). Its top edge **rises 7.96 mm** while
  the elbow sinks 6.55 mm. That is not how a TPU lattice takes a thumb. "No element turns inside out"
  was true but not the whole story. **1 321 of 53 248 elements GROW by more than 30 % under the press**
  (up to 2.1×). A press never grows a lattice, so that growth is a turn that the small-strain sim draws as
  a stretch. Two more causes: ν = 0.3 holds even where the cells are crushed, and the bottom is held fast.
  The walls there look shattered with the heat off (`VN_walls_g1_front_crest_zoom_rest_stepped_uncut.png`:
  their pull-back misses the steep field).
- **At your real weights (λ 1) it is better but not gone** (same sheet, bottom row): the end leans about
  half as far, but its top edge still rises **4.98 mm** while the elbow sinks 2.45 mm. So playing at your
  weights is a choice about the force, not a fix for the lean.
- Only core can fix the lean: #36 (large deformation), #41 (ν falling as the cells crush).
- **How much of your pad is past the tested curves:** 34 % of Group 1's part and 38 % of Group 2's are
  squeezed beyond the last tested strain (25 %). There the shape comes from the textbook densification
  law, not your filament's data.

### Your call (updated)
1. **Group 1's force.** Keep 2× your weights (the band's edge — the shape is deeper and leans more), or play
   every group at your real weights (λ 1) whenever the sim finds the part stiffer than core's columns? The
   lean stays either way until core #36 / #41.
2. **The densification past your data** — unchanged (34–38 % of your pad lives there): keep it, or test the
   filament to 60–70 % squish.

## Round 5 · batch N — a squish that folds realistically (★ read the verification pass above first)

Your words, on batch G's fold cut: **"Is there no way to fold realistically instead?"**

What I said I would do: solve the squish in STEPS, each voxel taking the stiffness core's tested curve
gives at ITS OWN squish, so the zones the linear sim over-squishes firm up and the full-size picture
stays smooth without the cut. That is built. **One thing I told you was wrong, and it matters:** I said
the curves already say TPU lattice stiffens as its cells close. For your filament they do not — see
"The curves" below. The stiffening the stepped sim needs comes from a textbook law past your data,
and the (i) says so.

Judged on YOUR project as you left it for round 5 (`his_project_0004_r5`, restored through
`AppModel.open`), on 0004 as saved, on C1's pads and on the M2 stand. **The app was NOT launched: nothing
here has been seen on a device or simulator.** The pictures are offscreen frames of the shipping renderer.

  G's linear sim, as today). The note beside the picker then reads **"Refining the squish… 3/8"** while the

  moment the refine starts, counting the step being solved.)

  verification pass.) **Your Group 1's top edge above the thumb rises into a crest** (frame `batch_n/N_his_r5_group-1_stepped_faces5_a100.png`). Two reasons, both
